shared_qns: apt29 has been observed crafting targeted spearphishing campaigns leveraging web links to a malicious dropper
apt34 has been observed targeting individuals through the use of booby-trapped job opportunity documents, delivered directly to the selected targets via linkedin messages
carbanak copies itself into "%system32%\com" with the name "svchost.exe"
carbanak injects its code into svchost.exe.
carbanak is a backdoor used by the attackers to compromise the victim's machine once the exploit, either in the spear phishing email or exploit kit, successfully executes its payload
carbanak uses the http protocol
cozy bear's preferred intrusion method is a broadly targeted spearphish campaign that typically includes web links to a malicious dropper.

cozyduke is a highly versatile, modular, malware "platform" whose functionality lies not in a single core component but in an array of modules that it may be instructed to download from its c&c server. these modules are used to selectively provide cozyduke with just the functionality deemed necessary for the mission at hand.
fin6 generally used either registry run keys
fin6 used an alternative extraction method to upload payment card data to a public file sharing service.
fin7 incorporated and adapted the notorious carbanak
fin7 phishing lures implements hidden sho%cut "les (lnk "les) to initiate the infection
in the months that followed, the duke group began to target victims with "o$ce monkeys"- and "efax"-themed emails, booby-trapped with a cozyduke payload.
many of the spearphishing emails sent by sandworm contained malware-laced documents that required user execution to deploy.
sandworm repeatedly accessed and browsed vles, ran malicious scripts, and searched compromised machines for credential vles
the dukes are known for launching their attacks by sending links to zip files, that contain malicious executables, hosted on legitimate compromised web servers.
this movement enabled fin6 to then inject lockergoga and ryuk ransomware
this would allow fin6 to escalate privileges in the system.
thousands of recipients being sent spear-phishing emails that contained links to compromised websites hosting cozyduke
we have observed apt29 use wmi to persist a backdoor and also store the powershell backdoor code.
what seems to be the core tools of these activities is a variant of anunak, remote backdoor, along with a visual basic script specially crafted with data exfiltration features
